title: A 1,500-year-old cliff temple now caps climbers at 2,475 a day | China Travel Expert
description:
A temple that hangs off a sheer cliff — and getting in just got harder.

The Hanging Temple (Xuankong Si) on Mount Heng in Datong, Shanxi, has clung to the rock for roughly 1,500 years, since the Northern Wei — its halls carried on timber beams socketed into the cliff face. From 1 April 2026 the scenic area caps daily ascents at 2,475 people (down from 3,275, with planned yearly cuts), and only about 1,200 of those tickets are sold online.

🧭 Expert Tip: grab one of the ~1,200 online tickets as early as you can, or arrive at opening to compete for the on-site allotment — the rest sell out fast in peak season.
